tagline: USSF reusable robotic spaceplane — multi-year classified orbital missions, the only US spaceplane operational after the Shuttle's retirement
description: Robotic mini-spaceplane (8.9 m long, ~5 t) built by Boeing Phantom Works for the USAF, transferred to the USSF in 2019. Launches vertically (Atlas V 501 for OTV-1 to 4 and OTV-6, Falcon 9 for OTV-5, Falcon Heavy for OTV-7) and lands horizontally on a runway (Vandenberg for OTV-1 to 3 and OTV-7, Kennedy's former Shuttle runway for OTV-4 to 6). Most payloads and orbital parameters are classified — known mission durations stretch from 224 days (OTV-1, 2010) to a record 908 days (OTV-6, 2020-2022). Declassified experiments include Hall-effect thruster tech demo, an AFRL radio-frequency communication test, and a 1 W solar-power-to-microwave-beaming experiment (PRAM, OTV-6). The first seven missions have landed; an eighth, USSF-36, launched on a Falcon 9 on 2025-08-22.
best_known_for: USSF reusable robotic spaceplane — classified multi-year orbital missions, post-Shuttle US spaceplane
